_about: Where to stay, base by base, from docs/research/07-lodging.md (researched 1 Oct 2026) and the plan doc's Where to sleep. Prices are JPY per night for the whole group of six, rounded; ryokan prices include dinner and breakfast. 'Verified' means read on an official site, Ikyu, Rakuten or a current guide; otherwise it is the sector pattern. Live availability for 31 Dec must be checked in a browser.

ground_rules.title: Decide the New Year anchor first
ground_rules.text: The three New Year nights (31 Dec–2 Jan) are the only scarce resource; everything else is still open. Most small ryokan load rooms six months out and their New Year plans sell out within weeks of posting in September. City hotels, apartment hotels and machiya do not have that cliff.

ground_rules.title: New Year surcharge
ground_rules.text: Ryokan: +50–100% on the normal per-person rate for 31 Dec–2 Jan, usually as a mandatory New Year plan with toshikoshi soba on the 31st and an osechi breakfast on 1 Jan (verified at Hakone Ginyu: +¥14,300 per person). City hotels: +30–80% on 31 Dec. Apartment hotels: roughly 1.5–2× the base rate.

ground_rules.title: Seven of us: four rooms, never one
ground_rules.text: Ryokan price per person. For three couples and Pedro's sister, ask for 3 rooms × 2 plus a single, or 2 rooms × 3 plus one room for a couple, the same plan and the same dinner sitting. Houses need three bedrooms and a sofa bed or a fourth room. One room for seven adults including a pregnant woman and two older parents is not advisable.

ground_rules.title: Beds, lifts, ground floors
ground_rules.text: Hotels always have lifts. Modern large ryokan do; small historic ones and machiya have steep stairs and bedrooms upstairs. Ask for a Japanese-Western room (和洋室): beds plus a tatami area. In a machiya, put her on the ground floor and check the bedrooms are heated.

ground_rules.title: Tell them she is pregnant
ground_rules.text: Say one guest is pregnant (妊娠中) and two are seniors: rooms near the lift, cooked courses instead of sashimi, low-sodium if needed, in-room dining if offered. Ryokan handle this routinely with three days' notice.

ground_rules.title: Refundable first
ground_rules.text: Hold city nights on official sites or Booking.com with free cancellation. Book the New Year ryokan on the strictest-but-still-refundable plan you can find (Ikyu and Rakuten show cancellation terms). Machiya brands charge in full at booking and refund to about 21–22 days out. Never hold more than two options per night.

ground_rules.title: The right channel
ground_rules.text: Hotels: official site or Booking.com. Ryokan: Ikyu (English, shows New Year plans), Rakuten Travel (about 10% cheaper than Booking), Jalan (Japanese only, most listings). A ryokan that shows sold out online often still has rooms by email for 2 rooms × 3. Machiya: the brand's own site.

ground_rules.title: Send the suitcases ahead
ground_rules.text: Yamato takkyubin hotel-to-hotel is about ¥2,000–2,800 per case, next day; allow an extra day from 28 Dec to 4 Jan. Travel the onsen nights with a daypack.

hotel.label: Hotel
hotel.blurb: Three rooms, or an apartment hotel with connecting units. A front desk for luggage forwarding and taxis.

rental.label: Whole house
rental.blurb: A machiya or apartment for six: a living room for the evenings, a kitchen and a washing machine. Usually beats three hotel rooms for three nights or more.

ryokan.label: Ryokan
ryokan.blurb: Dinner and breakfast included, a bath in the room. Priced per person. The nights where the stay itself is the point.

tokyo.why: Tokyo rentals are small and often far from stations. A front desk helps with luggage forwarding and taxis. Stay near a JR Yamanote line station; Asakusa, Ginza and Nihonbashi are calmer than Shinjuku over New Year.
tokyo.fit: Three double or twin rooms, two connecting apartments, or one 2–3 bedroom suite. Everything has lifts and beds.

candidates.name: MIMARU Tokyo Hatchobori
candidates.area: Hatchobori, between Tokyo Station and Ginza
candidates.what: 6-person Japanese apartment (two twins, a bunk and futon), or two connecting units with a door between them. Kitchen, washer.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, kitchen; the best fit for three couples who want one door between them.

candidates.name: MIMARU SUITES Tokyo Asakusa
candidates.what: Two-bedroom suites for six with a living room and kitchen.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. Senso-ji on the doorstep.

candidates.name: MIMARU SUITES Tokyo Nihombashi
candidates.what: Suites for 4–6 with kitchens, close to Tokyo Station for the 24 Dec shinkansen.

candidates.name: Tokyu Stay Ginza
candidates.what: Rooms with a kitchenette and a washer-dryer, three rooms for six.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, laundry in the room.

candidates.name: Oakwood Premier Tokyo
candidates.area: Marunouchi, on top of Tokyo Station
candidates.what: Serviced 1–2 bedroom apartments.

kanazawa.why: The longest stay. A shared living room for the evenings, a kitchen and a washing machine make it the mid-trip reset. Hotels are the fallback if the good machiya are gone.
kanazawa.fit: A machiya for exactly six with three bedrooms, or Hyatt House's kitchen rooms with connecting doors.
kanazawa.outlook: Open for hotels; tight for the nicest machiya. Omicho market closes 1–3 Jan, so our dates (24–28 Dec) are fine.

candidates.name: Machiya Residence Inn · Ainotsuji
candidates.what: A house for six: three bedrooms, two semi-double beds plus four futon, two bathrooms.
candidates.fit: Stairs; beds upstairs, futon can be laid downstairs for her. Paid in full at booking, refundable to 22 days.

candidates.name: Machiya Residence Inn · Hanatsume
candidates.what: Three bedrooms in the old samurai quarter.

candidates.name: Hyatt House Kanazawa
candidates.what: 92 rooms, 78 with kitchens, connecting rooms, laundry.

candidates.name: Kanazawa Machiya Kenroku
candidates.what: A whole machiya for up to six; cheaper per person from two nights.
candidates.price: From ¥39,000 for two, rises with group size

candidates.name: Dormy Inn or Tokyu Stay, three rooms
candidates.what: Business hotels with big public baths and free noodles at night.

takayama.why: Two nights rarely justify a rental's cleaning fee. Walking distance to the market and the old town matters on icy streets.
takayama.fit: Three rooms at a small hotel in the old town, or a machiya for six if it is cheaper for the two nights.
takayama.outlook: Open to tight. Nohi buses to Shirakawa-go thin out 29 Dec–3 Jan; we arrive on the 28th.

candidates.name: The Machiya Hotel Takayama
candidates.what: 14 rooms, group-friendly, in a restored merchant house.
candidates.fit: Check for a lift; ask for ground-floor rooms.

candidates.name: Machiya Inns & Hotels · Takayama houses
candidates.what: Restored houses that sleep 6–8, from the group that runs about 80 houses in Kyoto, Kanazawa and Takayama.

candidates.name: Hidatei Hanaougi
candidates.what: Ryokan with private baths and kaiseki; New Year's Eve in the gentler alternative.
candidates.price: ¥250,000–400,000 with meals, two or three rooms

candidates.name: Honjin Hiranoya Kachoan
candidates.what: Classic ryokan in the centre; the other candidate for a Takayama New Year's Eve.

gero.why: Restaurants close for New Year, so dinner and breakfast must be included. A flat town with footbaths, 45 minutes from Takayama and on the line to Kyoto.
gero.fit: Two rooms × 3 with the New Year plan: kaiseki on the 31st, osechi breakfast on 1 Jan. Ask for a room with its own bath, or book the private baths.
gero.outlook: Tight. New Year plans post on Jalan, Rakuten and Ikyu in September–October; the best-known houses clear within weeks. Book this month, and email if a site shows sold out.

candidates.name: Yunoshimakan
candidates.area: On the hill above the town, shuttle from the station
candidates.what: A 1931 wooden building (registered cultural property), four free private baths, dinner served in the room.
candidates.price: About ¥35,000–45,000 per person with meals, plus the New Year uplift
candidates.fit: Historic building with steps; ask for a room near the lift and dinner in the room.

candidates.name: Suimeikan
candidates.what: Large ryokan with three buildings, private baths to book, some rooms with their own onsen, Western-Japanese rooms.
candidates.price: About ¥30,000–45,000 per person with meals, plus the New Year uplift
candidates.fit: Lift, beds available, the easiest for the parents and her.

candidates.name: Bosenkan
candidates.what: Only about eight rooms have open-air baths and they sell out first.
candidates.fit: Ask for a bath-in-room pair of rooms.

kyoto.why: A living room for the evenings over New Year, when most restaurants are closed 1–3 Jan and department-store basements reopen on the 2nd. Stock the kitchen on arrival. An apartment hotel is the fallback.
kyoto.fit: One machiya for 6–9 with three bedrooms, or a MIMARU SUITES apartment, or two Nazuna houses.
kyoto.outlook: Open for houses and apartment hotels; tight for the famous machiya brands; gone for Nazuna's New Year dinner-plan rooms (¥277,400 per room for 1–3).

candidates.name: Machiya Residence Inn · Mizunoha
candidates.what: A house for six: two beds, two semi-doubles and two futon.
candidates.fit: Stairs; beds mostly upstairs, futon can be made up downstairs. Welcome Desk check-in, luggage delivered to the house for ¥500 an item.

candidates.name: Machiya Residence Inn · Hanatoki or Fujinoma
candidates.what: Houses for eight: two queens plus four futon, more room to spread out.

candidates.name: MIMARU SUITES Kyoto Shijo
candidates.what: Apartment-hotel suites for 4–6 with kitchen and laundry; a front desk.

candidates.name: Rinn Rokujo
candidates.what: Rinn's smaller machiya for six.

candidates.name: Nazuna Kyoto Gosho
candidates.what: Two small luxury houses; the Tsubaki St New Year plan is ¥277,400 per room for 1–3 with an 11-course wagyu dinner (free cancellation to 21 days).

hakone.why: A ryokan with an open-air bath in each room, so all three couples get the same room and she controls the temperature and time. Kaiseki for dinner; ask for a cooked-only menu for her.
hakone.fit: Two rooms × 3, ideally Western or Japanese-Western rooms. Large modern houses have lifts.
hakone.outlook: Our dates (5–7 Jan) are after the New Year rush: tight at the top houses, open at the mid-size ones. 31 Dec would have been gone.

candidates.name: Gora Hanaougi
candidates.what: Open-air bath in every room; dinner and breakfast included.
candidates.price: About ¥45,000–55,000 per person with meals (half-board rooms for two about US$570–615)
candidates.fit: Lift, beds in some rooms; the first choice if we go to Hakone.

candidates.name: Kitanokaze Saryo
candidates.what: Open-air bath in every room, near the Pola and glass museums.

candidates.name: Hakone Ginyu
candidates.what: Private rotenburo on every terrace, Western rooms for 1–3, lobby on the top floor with a lift.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. Email for two rooms.

candidates.name: Hakone Kowakien Ten-yu
candidates.what: Modern, large, Western-Japanese rooms, infinity bath.
candidates.fit: Lift, beds. The easiest fit for the parents.

candidates.name: Yoshiike Ryokan
candidates.what: Big garden, rooms up to six, lift.

candidates.name: Gora Kadan
candidates.what: A former imperial retreat, three Michelin Keys, open-air baths in the suites.

kinosaki.why: The town is the baths; a ryokan gives the yukata, the bath pass and the crab kaiseki. Choose one with a private bath for her because the public ones run hot.
kinosaki.fit: Two or three rooms; the Nishimuraya houses have Western beds and lifts.
kinosaki.outlook: Tight. Crab season plus New Year is Kinosaki's peak and two-night plans are common; our dates (5–7 Jan) are just after the rush.

candidates.name: Nishimuraya Hotel Shogetsutei
candidates.what: 98 rooms, Western and Western-Japanese rooms, lift, crab kaiseki; a ¥2,000 per room voucher for direct booking.

candidates.name: Nishimuraya Honkan
candidates.what: 1860, Relais & Châteaux, snow-crab kaiseki.

candidates.name: Morizuya, Tsutaya or Mikuniya
candidates.what: Mid-size family inns on the canal.

yudanaka.why: A ryokan dinner after the monkeys; Shibu's bath-hopping street is the evening.
yudanaka.fit: Two rooms at a larger inn with a lift; the six-room village inns have stairs and are tight.
yudanaka.outlook: Open at the larger houses for 23–25 Dec.

candidates.name: Biyunoyado
candidates.what: Large modern ryokan with a lift and Western-Japanese rooms; takes families at New Year.

candidates.name: Shibu Onsen village inns
candidates.what: Small historic inns with the key to the nine public baths.

okuhida.why: The snow baths are the point; dinner is at the inn because there is nothing else.
okuhida.fit: Two rooms at an inn with a lift and an open-air bath.

candidates.name: Hirayu or Shinhotaka inns
candidates.what: Rotenburo in the snow; the official association lists the inns.

okayama.why: A station hotel for two nights makes Himeji, Kurashiki and the Naoshima ferry easy.

candidates.name: Hotel Granvia Okayama
candidates.what: The station hotel.

candidates.name: Benesse House Park, Naoshima
candidates.what: The art hotel's lift wing; museum closures around New Year to check.

hiroshima.why: Two nights near the station or the Peace Park.

candidates.name: Sheraton Grand or Hotel Granvia Hiroshima
candidates.what: Station hotels for a short stay.

kawaguchiko.why: The lake is the point: a room on the north or east shore that looks straight at Fuji, so the first light on the mountain happens from bed. A lake hotel with beds and a lift suits the parents and her; the hoto houses cover lunch, and dinner is at the hotel or in town.
kawaguchiko.fit: Three rooms for two at a lakeside hotel with beds and a lift, Fuji-side rooms asked for by name. Konansou's lake-view rooms take up to six but are tatami only, so only with its Western-Japanese wing.
kawaguchiko.outlook: Our dates (5–7 Jan) are after the first-sunrise rush: open at the hotels, tight at Konansou and the top houses. 31 Dec would have been gone.

candidates.name: Fujikawaguchiko Onsen Ubuya
candidates.what: Every room faces the lake and Fuji; in-room open-air baths in the better rooms; kaiseki dinner.
candidates.fit: Lift, Western-Japanese rooms with beds. The first one to ask, for the Fuji view from the room; not yet checked on an official site.

candidates.name: Fuji View Hotel
candidates.what: The classic 1936 lakeside hotel: Western beds, a garden on the water, restaurants.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. The easiest fit for the parents.

candidates.name: Hotel Mystays Fuji Onsen Resort
candidates.what: Modern, beds, lift, onsen with a Fuji view.

candidates.name: Konansou
candidates.what: Tamayura lake-view rooms for 1–6, lift, rooftop foot bath with the Fuji view; half-board.
candidates.price: From ¥70,400 for two half-board; about ¥200,000 for six in normal season
candidates.fit: Lift; tatami only, so ask for the Western-Japanese wing or a bed. Verified on Ikyu.

candidates.name: Fufu Kawaguchiko
candidates.what: All-suite, beds, an onsen in every room.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, in-room onsen for her.

candidates.name: Hoshinoya Fuji
candidates.what: Glamping cabins facing Fuji, beds, outdoor fires; three cabins for six.
candidates.fit: Beds; a buggy up the hill; New Year plans usually two-night minimum.
